note: R114-B frozen-window run — same fixture but ENDLIST deliberately late (wall 38-45s) while media supply (16 segs) exhausts ~wall 30. Demonstrates: when a rolling live playlist stops offering new segments (window contains only already-consumed frags, no ENDLIST), hls.js signals EOS early rather than spinning forever.

stallBeforeEnd.cause: buffer exhausted at live edge — no new segments were being produced (fixture content exhausted)

variant_b_reset_timestamps.note: An earlier run used segments encoded with -reset_timestamps 1 (each TS restarts at PTS 0) — at the DISCONTINUITY boundary playback stalled ~21s. With continuous-PTS segments (real live encoder behavior) the same boundary crosses with zero stall. Verdict: fixture artifact, not an app/hls.js defect; documented so future fixtures keep -reset_timestamps 0.

appErrors: none — no hlsRecovery restart triggered, quality selector stayed ['auto','0'], no error surfaced to UI log beyond normal lifecycle
